To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a single image volume estimation method can be built based on simple shape descriptors, (2) a single image based volume estimation method can also be built based on a database with known volumes, and (3) both methods perform better than the current state-of-the-art methods used in clinical practice.

(i) the proposed regression-based methods perform better than spherical and ellipsoidal volume models, (ii) the proposed example-based method outperforms the proposed regression-based method, (iii) the example-based methods are more sensitive to the quality of the training data, and (iv) all the proposed methods perform better than the methods used in clinical practice.

(i) a single 2-dimensional image can be used to estimate the volume of pancreatic islets; (ii) the proposed volume estimation methods perform significantly better, in most cases, than the methods currently in use, based on simple spherical and ellipsoidal models; and (iii) the proposed regression-based methods can be used to obtain a rough estimation of the islet volume, which can be used in clinical practice to decide whether to perform the more time-consuming and expensive stereological volume estimation
